# Introduction

`occuFitR` provides goodness-of-fit (GOF) tests and diagnostic tools for single-season occupancy models fitted using `unmarked`.

This vignette demonstrates how to use the package to assess model fit, examine bootstrap results and investigate patterns in site-level residuals. A simulated dataset is used throughout so that the example can be reproduced without requiring external data.

# Simulating occupancy data

We first simulate detection histories for 100 sites surveyed on five occasions. Occupancy and detection probabilities are assumed constant across sites and survey occasions.

```{r simulate}
library(unmarked)
library(occuFitR)

set.seed(123)

n_sites <- 100
n_visits <- 5

# Simulate occupancy states
z <- rbinom(n_sites, size = 1, prob = 0.6)

# Simulate detection histories
y <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = n_sites,
  ncol = n_visits
)

for (j in seq_len(n_visits)) {
  y[, j] <- rbinom(
    n_sites,
    size = 1,
    prob = z * 0.35
  )
}

# Create unmarkedFrame
umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y)
```

# Fitting an occupancy model

We fit a single-season occupancy model with constant occupancy and detection probabilities using `unmarked::occu()`.

```{r model}
fit <- occu(
  ~ 1 ~ 1,
  data = umf
)

summary(fit)
```

# Assessing goodness of fit

We can assess model fit using `occu_gof()`. The function calculates three complementary GOF statistics and uses a parametric bootstrap to generate reference distributions under the fitted model.

```{r gof}
withCallingHandlers(
  gof <- occu_gof(fit, n_boot = 5, seed = 123),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("\n--- Error details ---\n")
    print(conditionMessage(e))
    cat("\n--- Calls at point of failure ---\n")
    print(sys.calls())
    stop(e)
  }
)
```

The number of bootstrap replicates can be increased for a more precise assessment. A smaller number is used here to keep the vignette quick to build.

## Test statistics and p-values

The observed values of the three GOF statistics are available through the `statistic` component:

```{r statistics}
gof$statistic
```

Bootstrap p-values are available through:

```{r p-values}
gof$p_value
```

Small p-values indicate that the observed test statistic is unusually large relative to the bootstrap distribution, providing evidence of lack of fit.

## Bootstrap distributions

The bootstrap distributions can also be examined directly:

```{r bootstrap}
head(gof$bootstrap)
```

# Examining site-level residuals

The `psi_p` and `p` statistics provide site-level residuals that can be used to investigate patterns in model fit.

```{r residuals}
head(gof$residuals$psi_p)
head(gof$residuals$p)
```

## Residuals against site covariates

`plot_residuals()` produces diagnostic plots of site-level residuals against site covariates. Numeric covariates are displayed with GAM smooths, while categorical covariates are displayed using boxplots.

For example, residuals from the occupancy and detection probability statistic can be plotted against the site covariates:

```{r covariate-plots, eval=FALSE}
plot_residuals(
  gof,
  test = "psi_p"
)
```

## Spatial residual patterns

When spatial coordinates are available in the site covariates, `plot_spatial_residuals()` can be used to investigate spatial patterns in residuals.

For example, with projected coordinates:

```{r spatial-plots, eval=FALSE}
plot_spatial_residuals(
  gof,
  test = "psi_p",
  coords = c("easting", "northing"),
  crs = 27700
)
```

A user-supplied polygon can also be used to define the prediction area through the `boundary` argument.

# Further information

See the package documentation for details of the individual GOF statistics and diagnostic functions:
